rules.rule: Prefer the official VyrnForge component or framework surface for the selected consumer framework before creating a one-off custom control.
rules.reason: Keeps UI semantics, accessibility, styling, and behavior aligned across supported surfaces.

rules.rule: Use @vyrnforge/ui-data-grid only for data-management tables where its current React-only support and alpha maturity are appropriate.
rules.reason: UniversalDataGrid is a specialized advanced capability, not a generic layout component or a claim of current multi-framework grid parity.

rules.rule: Do not use DataGrid as generic layout.
rules.reason: Use VyrnForge layout primitives and composition patterns instead.

rules.rule: Use Button for primary or business actions.
rules.reason: Visible labels are clearer for important actions.

rules.rule: Use IconButton or ToolbarButton for repeated utility actions when those components are available on the selected surface.
rules.reason: They provide consistent compact action semantics and styling.

rules.rule: Every icon-only button needs an accessible name such as aria-label when the surrounding semantics do not already provide one.
rules.reason: Assistive-technology users need a text name for the control.

rules.rule: Use VyrnForge CSS custom properties and semantic tokens for styling customization.
rules.reason: VyrnForge theming is token-driven and portable across supported surfaces.

rules.rule: Do not add MUI, Tailwind, Radix, TanStack, Redux, Zustand, styled-components, Emotion, large icon libraries, or similar frameworks unless explicitly approved.
rules.reason: VyrnForge is native-owned, dependency-minimal, and application-store agnostic.

rules.rule: Keep application data fetching, caching, authentication, authorization, routing, persistence, and business workflow execution outside VyrnForge packages.
rules.reason: VyrnForge owns reusable UI semantics; consuming applications own business/runtime semantics.

rules.rule: Check current component, package, framework, and maturity status before using or recommending a planned or target capability.
rules.reason: Canonical metadata may describe both current implementation and accepted target state.

rules.rule: Before using a VyrnForge component or contract, check the canonical API and metadata sources relevant to the selected framework and task.
rules.reason: Public API and canonical metadata define usage; generated or AI-facing views must not invent missing semantics.

rules.rule: Do not use undocumented internal APIs or deep package imports unless explicitly asked and the architecture permits it.
rules.reason: Only documented public entrypoints, props, tokens, events, methods, and adapter contracts are supported consumer API.

rules.rule: Use the canonical component property, event, composition, form, model, ref, accessibility, and framework mappings before adding framework-specific APIs.
rules.reason: Shared contracts prevent supported framework surfaces from drifting into separate component libraries.

rules.rule: Distinguish verified consumer evidence, current shipped packages, accepted target packages, migration state, and explicit exceptions when describing framework support.
rules.reason: Framework support claims must follow current package/release metadata and accepted architecture rather than stale planning assumptions.

rules.rule: Treat advanced capabilities such as grids, trees, visualization, complex editors, and spatial UI as optional modules unless an approved architecture says otherwise; do not pull their weight or engines into the common foundation.
rules.reason: Capability depth should not make unrelated VyrnForge consumers pay unnecessary dependency, bundle, CSS, or runtime cost.

rules.rule: Do not start deferred advanced capability implementation merely because it is valid long-term VyrnForge scope; follow the active roadmap and approved architecture work.
rules.reason: The S10-S15 multi-framework distribution program remains the current critical path until its gates close.

rules.rule: Follow current canonical package boundaries and require a dedicated architecture decision before adding new advanced-module or framework dependency edges.
rules.reason: Shared foundations must remain dependency-minimal and must not acquire reverse dependencies on renderers or optional advanced modules.

rules.rule: Prefer task- and framework-scoped AI context derived from canonical metadata instead of loading or copying the entire VyrnForge documentation set.
rules.reason: ADR-010 requires bounded, deterministic AI context with no parallel source of product semantics.
